data: How was the identification rate calculated, and how does it affect the results?

The identification rate is calculated based on the evolution of the identification rate as a function of α and β, when the first and second eigenresiduals (µ1(n) and µ2(n)) are combined according to Equations (5) and (6). The results show an increasing trend for both α and β, indicating that the identification rate improves as these parameters increase. The relationship between the two graphs suggests that there is a positive correlation between α and β, meaning that higher values of one parameter generally correspond to higher values of the other. This can be inferred from the fact that the curves in both graphs are positively sloped and appear to be moving in the same direction.
